title: PUT used for partial update — method semantics violated
expected_feedback: Standard (S1, nature [P] — §8.1: FAIL): two method/status defects. (1) PUT means replace the entire resource; a server that merges absent fields has PATCH semantics behind a PUT verb, so a client that legitimately omits a field to clear it gets the opposite of what the method promises. Use PATCH for partial update and reserve PUT for full replacement — or keep PUT and require the complete representation. (2) A successful create returns 200; it should be 201. Note the boundary: the missing `Location` header on that 201 is a [D] recommendation and not part of this finding — RFC 9110 §15.3.2 says the target URI identifies the new resource when Location is absent.
